sources.entry: Syntax Highlight - Quick Look extension for highlight source code files. - ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS Quick Look extension and companion app that previews source code files with syntax highlighting, powered by the embedded Highlight engine.
summary.what_it_does: The app provides a Quick Look extension for macOS 12 and later that renders source files with syntax highlighting using Highlight, with support for a very large list of languages and many plain-text or extensionless files. It offers rendering settings for RTF or HTML engines, color schemes for light and dark appearance, fonts, word wrap, line numbers, and tab handling. Per-format options allow extra highlight arguments, preprocessors (for example, beautifying JSON before rendering), and forced syntax selection. It can optionally connect to external Language Server executables for hover, semantic tokens and syntax errors, and can highlight lines changed since the last git or mercurial commit. A syntax_highlight_cli command line tool supports batch conversion to HTML or RTF.
use_cases: Quick Look preview of source code files on macOS
Syntax highlighting for code in Finder previews
Batch converting source files to HTML or RTF from the command line
Viewing git or mercurial changed lines in a code preview
Previewing Xcode, plist, or XML files with highlighting
Previewing extensionless shell or config files
how_to_run: Download the precompiled Syntax Highlight.app from the releases page and move it to Applications
Launch the app once so the system registers the Quick Look extension
Enable it under System Preferences > Extensions > Quick Look
notable: Supports a very long list of languages and file types, including AppleScript decompilation via osadecompile and plist decompilation via plutil
Optional external Language Server Protocol integration with hover and semantic tokens
Preprocessor option lets an external program transform a file before highlighting
Command line tool syntax_highlight_cli for batch conversion
Version control highlighting for git and mercurial
caveats: Requires macOS 12.0 or later; macOS 11 and 10.15 must use version 2.1.30
Some extensions such as .ts, .dart, .json (on Apple Silicon Ventura), and .plist (on Catalina) are reserved by macOS and cannot be handled
Custom file formats cannot be added manually; they must be added at compile time, and modifying the app breaks its code signature
